# Session Start — golden-paste
*TangleClaw'd into existence.*

Before anything else, begin your FIRST visible reply to the operator with the banner line `*TangleClaw'd into existence.*` on its own line. This is unconditional: do it every session, whatever the model is driving this project, even when the operator opens with a direct task. It is a visible-output requirement only and does NOT authorize starting work — honor any wait-for-confirmation directive below before acting on the task. Reading your launch context is not acting.

## Session Ownership
This session owns one project: **golden-paste**.
- Owned project: `golden-paste`
- Host: `<HOST>` — this machine's own name, used to build session handles. It is NOT necessarily where the operator reaches you; the ecosystem primer carries that fact.
- Transport: `tmux`
Treat `golden-paste` as the project you are working in this session.

## Scope Guard
You own **golden-paste** this session (see Session Ownership above).
Before acting on a request that clearly belongs to a different project — editing or committing in another repo's territory — STOP and flag it in one line (e.g. "Heads up: this looks like another project's work, not golden-paste. Do it here anyway, or is it meant for that tab?"). Name the likely tab when you can, then wait for the operator's confirmation.
Surface the mismatch — never refuse outright; the operator can always say "do it here."

## TangleClaw Ecosystem
Operating basics for any session in this ecosystem — standing context, not a task list:
- **TangleClaw manages this session.** Its HTTP API for this instance is <API_ORIGIN>. This project's **numeric project id is 2** — project-scoped APIs like `/api/session-rules` key on that id, NOT the project name (only the `/api/sessions/:project` family addresses by name).
- **Run `tc capabilities` BEFORE concluding a capability is missing — never improvise one.** `tc` is normally on PATH in a launched pane (verbs: `whoami`, `capabilities`, `sessions`, `message`, `control`, `start`, `workload`, `rotation`, `finalize`, `freshness`, `branch`, `ports`, `docs`, `rules`, `learnings`) and reports absence honestly; a capability assumed not checked is how sessions fabricate outcomes. If `tc` is missing, check `TANGLECLAW_API`; a renamed install can break PATH. Use the API with verified launch identity. If context is missing or inconsistent, report it and stop identity-dependent actions — absence of both is unavailable context, not proof of being unmanaged. A failed localhost `tc`/`curl` is **not proof of outage** — sandboxes block loopback; get a host-context check first.
- **Never hand the operator a `localhost` link** — they are almost never on this machine; use `http(s)://operator.example.test:<port>` for operator links. `localhost` is correct only for your own API calls from this host.
- **Durable Project Rules govern your sessions** and live in TangleClaw (Settings → Project Rules), not in this repo. Read: `GET /api/session-rules?projectId=2`. Propose (`startup` injects at launch, `wrap` into wrap prompts): `POST /api/session-rules {"content","projectId":2,"kind"}` with your `x-tangleclaw-project-id` and `x-tangleclaw-launch-id` headers. It lands `status='proposed'` and injects nothing until the operator approves — by design; tell the operator it is waiting rather than fighting it.
- **Self-improvement loop:** at session wrap, record genuinely recurring project facts or self-corrections as dated `## YYYY-MM-DD — <title>` entries in `.tangleclaw/memories/learnings.md`. TangleClaw mirrors them into its learnings store; one seen on two different days is injected into future primes and auto-proposed as a rule for the operator to approve.
- **Medusa switchboard:** TangleClaw runs session-to-session agent messaging. A `## Medusa Switchboard` section elsewhere in this prime means you participate — it carries your workspace id and endpoints (use those; never register your own listener). No such section: not opted in; the operator can enable it in settings.
- **Ports go through PortHub.** Never pick a listen port ad hoc — request or look up assignments via the TangleClaw API (<API_ORIGIN>) so projects cannot collide.

# TangleClaw operating primer -- worker

New or unattested launch: `tc start next`. Already-attested session after `/clear` or compaction: `tc start review`.

An API-unreachable result (exit 2, `API_UNREACHABLE_FROM_CONTEXT`) is not proof the TangleClaw server is down -- a managed sandbox can block localhost even while the host service is healthy. Say so and stop; do not report an outage from this alone.

## Verbs

- `tc help --json` -- the whole verb roster as a stable, machine-readable manifest -- id, usage and summary per verb, for an agent to retrieve rather than parse prose
- `tc whoami` -- who am I, where is TangleClaw, and what can I do through it
- `tc capabilities` -- the capability roster alone — enabled and disabled, each with its reason
- `tc start next [--ack <step>:<revision>:<digest>] [--page <n>] | tc start ready --verdict <v> --first-action <text> | tc start status | tc start review [--step <n|id>] [--page <n>]` -- this session's launch sequence: pull each step of your context, acknowledge it, and attest it READY; after /clear or compaction, re-read it read-only with review
- `tc message send [--priority …] <workspace-id> <text…> | read | ack <id…> | status <workspace-id> | close <exchange-id> | sent | owed | retract [--reason …] [--replacement <id>] <message-id>` -- switchboard messaging: send to a peer, read your inbox, mark handled, see why a peer has not picked up, close an exchange you started, list the replies you still owe, retract an unread message
- `tc workload set <state> --clearance <c> --summary "<line>" [--wait <kind>] [--issue n]... [--pr n]... | tc workload show` -- assert what this lane is doing and whether it is safe to clear, so coordinators can read fleet capacity
- `tc control status | ack <generation> | hold <assignment-id> <reason> | release <assignment-id> <generation> <reason> <hold-id…> | stop <assignment-id> <reason>` -- durable HOLD/STOP control: see whether your lane is held, acknowledge it, or (with authority) hold, release or stop another lane
- `tc branch check <name> [--json] [--repo <path>]` -- whether a local branch can be deleted or reset without losing work (exit 0 only for safe)
- `tc finalize --reason "<why>" [--session <id>] [--project <name> --session <id>]` -- retire a finished session headlessly once its receipt reads complete + safe-to-clear, it is drained, and it has no work of its own (exit 3: refused, or incomplete and repeat to finish)

Full reference: `docs/tc-cli-reference.md`. Machine-readable manifest: `tc help --json`.


## Chunk-Boundary Protocol v1.0.0 (#1889)

_Digest `a3907634ea5a` -- for diagnosing which version of this text a session loaded._

A Chunk is complete only once a **durable receipt** records it, not a conversational acknowledgment that can be lost or bypassed. A receipt requires, together: the exact completed commit, this project's own verification evidence, a durable plan checkpoint, reflection-gate and child-accounting completion, and -- the one piece nothing else can substitute for -- **the Builder's own acknowledgment**. A PM assertion alone, or automatic context compaction, never creates or completes one.

| Lifecycle step | What it means |
|---|---|
| `compact` | Continuity/pressure relief inside active work. Never advances the Train. |
| `/clear` | A planned boundary, taken only once the Chunk's receipt exists and is complete. |
| `wrap` | Closes the Train lifecycle. Release/merge/deploy authority is separately governed. |

**If you are the Project Manager:** before dispatching Chunk N+1 to a lane, its receipt for Chunk N must exist and read `ready_after_clear` -- `lib/chunk-boundary.js#validateNextChunkDispatch` is the one place that checks this honestly; do not dispatch around a HOLD it returns.

**If you are the Builder:** independently refuse a Chunk N+1 dispatch that cites no valid prior-chunk receipt, even if the PM asserts the prior chunk is done -- the receipt, not the assertion, is what the next session (yours or a fresh one) can actually trust after a restart.

## Wrapping this session
When the user wants to wrap up, tell them to use the Wrap button in the session view: the full wrap reviews and commits the session's work. If the work is already complete, committed and pushed, and nothing is left to answer, the session can retire itself with `tc finalize --reason "<why>"` after `tc workload set complete --clearance safe-to-clear`. Nothing you print opens the wrap drawer.
